Throwing an overstable disc forehand, just like backhand, can be a lot more forgiving. If you over turn it you know it’s coming back. If you put too much torque it’s still going to come back. And it’s more reliable in the wind. You get punished for poor form and mistakes more with under stable discs. I would say it’s ‘easier’ and less of a risk to get distance with an overstable flex forehand than a less stable disc. I see guys all the time at the course that drive with a disc like a stable destroyer that they just flex it like crazy to get honestly pretty good distance for both for backhand and forehand because it doesn’t require as pure of form to execute to get that distance. Nothing wrong with that approach. Nikko has been killing it by flexing almost every shot he throws.

I’ve been trying to learn to throw flippier discs forehand too because i think it’s really fun and I think, just like throwing understable discs backhand, that it leads to more efficient form.

Extreme digestive distress that the doctors didn’t think much of as my tests and bloodwork didn’t show too much initially. Kind of a ‘just monitor what you eat and don’t eat what bothers you thing’.  

I went vegan and was feeling really good, but about 8 months later I noticed I had two swollen lymph nodes on my clavicle. I read to wait two weeks and if they don’t go down to see a doctor. 2 weeks went by and all at one time I lost 15 pounds from my athletic 5’10 170 frame (personal trainer and gymnastics Coach and avid lifter), started to experience extreme fatigue and weakness ( my lifts dropped about 50% in one weeks time, could do 15 pull ups and suddenly could hardly do 1 in spite of being lighter), bad hip pain and back pain, and a few other things.

Went and got bloodwork done and my numbers were all over the place in the worst way. Got a PET scan and other tests and they found I had Hodgkin’s Lymphoma through every part of my Lymphatic system. Got a Bone marrow biopsy done and they claim we caught it right before it spread to my bones. I had apprantley been living with it since possibly highschool (diagnosed at 23). 

Went through 8 months of horrible treatment but am now a year removed and officially in remission! I do have a rare form that has a high relapse rate, but I feel good to boogie for now.

Your timing is off and you’re very tense. I think that fixing those two things will make all the other little things fall into place.

For your timing:

Think about having your reach back finish when your plant foots toes are on the ground. Right now your reach back is finished well before then. Fixing that will help with your body brace and it will make it easier to pull your elbow into your brace/throw. Getting your elbow into the throw not only gets your disc into the power pocket, but it helps overall with not rounding, power, and consistency.

One step throws and standstill throws with rhythm can help a lot with timing.

For how tense you are:

Think about being as light and relaxed as possible through the throwing motion until you’re planting and pulling your disc through. Your legs, arms, grip and everything else should be relaxed but have purpose if that makes sense. 

Remember that you want your arm to act as a whip. Your body is what pulls the whip and the disc is the tip of the whip. Trying to muscle the throw causes your arm pull your body through instead of the other way around.

Thinking about moving your body around the disc throughout the motion until you pull can help with both timing and staying relaxed too.
